home.title: {siteName} — A sensory trail for blind and visually impaired people, Sacred Valley of the Incas
home.description: An educational and sensory trail being developed for blind and visually impaired people, with their families, friends and companions, in the Sacred Valley of the Incas, Cusco, Peru.
home.heroAlt: Poster of the project. A person in a knit hat and orange poncho walks with a white cane on a stone path beside a wooden fence, passing a two-story stone house where a woman and a child stand. Two people plant in a green field among chickens, and two rheas stand by a stone wall, with snow-capped mountains behind. The poster reads: INCA BRAILLE TRAIL — GUIDING YOUR STEPS THROUGH THE CYCLE OF LIFE. A sign says the project is under construction and that volunteers are urgently needed.
home.tagline:
First of its kind educational and sensory journey through the cycle of life and Andean agriculture

Designed for blind and visually impaired people.

Sighted visitors can choose to wear a blindfold for the trail. By briefly setting sight aside, they can tune in to the sounds, textures, and scents of the farm, discovering details they might usually miss and feeling more connected to the natural world.

boxes.title: What Is the Inca Braille Trail?

content.lead: A Journey Through Nature, Education and the Senses

content: Located in the beautiful Sacred Valley of the Incas, Cusco, Peru, the Inca Braille Trail is an educational and sensory experience being developed specifically for blind and visually impaired people, together with their families, friends and companions.
Our vision is to create a welcoming place where visitors can enjoy nature, learn, explore and share meaningful experiences, free of charge through the support of sponsors and donations.

The trail is designed to stimulate the senses through touch, smell, sound and taste. Visitors will discover the textures of plants, the fragrances of herbs and flowers, the sounds of nature and the many wonderful experiences the natural world has to offer.

boxes.title: The Cycle of Life – Learning from Pachamama
content: At the heart of our philosophy is respect for Pachamama, Mother Earth, and the understanding that all living things are connected.
Through our educational journey, The Cycle of Life, visitors will discover how the needs of plants closely reflect our own.
A tiny seed needs nourishment, water, warmth and care to grow, just as we need nutritious food, clean water, sunlight and a healthy environment to thrive.
Plants draw nutrients from healthy soil and energy from sunlight, while we depend on the food they produce for our own energy, growth and wellbeing.

content.lead: Healthy soil nurtures healthy plants. Healthy plants nourish healthy people.

content: Animals also play an essential role in this cycle. From honeybees pollinating flowers to birds spreading seeds, and farm animals providing natural manure that enriches the soil, every creature contributes to the balance of nature.
These nutrients return to the earth, helping new plants grow and completing the beautiful cycle that connects plants, animals and people.

Along the journey, visitors will explore traditional Andean and ancient Inca agricultural practices alongside modern sustainable farming. We emphasize the importance of preserving native seeds, composting, protecting biodiversity and growing nutritious food without relying on harmful agricultural chemicals.
Our goal is to demonstrate that caring for the earth and producing healthy food can be simple, sustainable and accessible to everyone.

boxes.title: A Place for Everyone to Connect – The Spirit of Ayni
content: At the heart of the Inca Braille Trail is the ancient Andean principle of Ayni, meaning reciprocity — the belief that through giving, receiving and supporting one another, we create stronger, more compassionate communities.

Our trail is more than an educational experience. It is a place where blind and visually impaired people, their families, friends and companions can come together, share experiences, build friendships and celebrate life.
We also hope to encourage sighted visitors to better understand the everyday challenges faced by people with visual impairments, developing greater awareness, empathy and respect.
Through shared experiences, we want people to recognize that everyone has something valuable to offer and that we all have something to learn from one another.
Just as we nurture the earth and the earth nurtures us, through kindness, compassion and reciprocity, we nurture one another.

content.lead: This is the spirit of Ayni, and the heart of the Inca Braille Trail.

boxes.title: Help build the trail
content:
WE NEED YOUR HELP!!!
Families are welcome!
Help bring the Inca Braille Trail to life
WHY ?
This Inca Braille Trail is the first of its kind with NFC/QR code technology to make education and sensory activities to the blind, general visually impaired and also to allow the general public with sight to enhance their other senses more intensely through sight deprivation.
Our hope is that once you experience this you will feel more compassion for those less fortunate and recognise your own sensitivity to your own inner magic.
Funds raised will go directly toward providing a free day at the Inca Braille Trail for people who are blind or have low vision, along with their families and carers. The day includes return transport from Cusco, lunch, and a gift to take home.
Often the careers and family are forgotten so lets celebrate this together by helping make this a fun and   ongoing event of a lifetime for all.

Help needed:
-Small stone paths
-Basic fencing
-Cooking
-Social Media
-General cleaning
-Raking
-planting aromatics

list: Volunteers staying with us and working full days: Accommodation, breakfast, lunch and dinner provided.
Transport: Available from an agreed collection point.

content: Contact us to arrange dates and find tasks suited to your abilities.

work.lead: We are working hard to build the trails. Here are a few pictures of our work.
work.photo1: Three people build a stone wall on a dirt slope. A gray-bearded man kneels and holds a measuring tape. A bald man carries a long wooden log. Another person in a hat bends over the stones. A green container and mountains are behind them.
work.photo2: The same stone wall. The gray-bearded man holds the measuring tape. The person in the hat works on the stones. The bald man, with a red glove, pulls a long-handled tool.
work.photo3: Three men work beside a low stone wall. A gray-bearded man in a black shirt with an orange 23 and tall rubber boots smiles at the camera. A man in a wide hat points to the side. A bald man with red gloves bends over a rake. A green container, trees and mountains are behind them.
work.photo4: Tools hang from a wire on a pale wall: a small cultivator, three trowels, two pairs of pliers and a handsaw. A garden fork stands on the dirt next to a blue tarp and an orange bag.
work.video: The same work in motion: measuring the ground, setting the stone wall and moving timber, with mountains behind.

educational.title: Educational trail — {siteName}
educational.description: A walk that teaches how food grows, returns to the soil as compost, and becomes food again.
educational.heroLine: Here you learn the whole path through the cycle of life.
educational.heroAlt: Two hands hold small green fruits among leaves. One fruit rests in an open palm.
educational.lead:
Download the app: Then the experience begins....
Two options:
1: Visually Impaired: Audio version
2: Sighted: QR/NFC scan at stations..

All Junction points have Braille information cards.
1. Visually Impaired: Audio versionYou will have a trained volunteer who will accompany you if you do not have a sighted guide. The guided audio will take you on a journey through 20 stations of information. There will be 4 rest points along the way. At each rest point you will have to answer 5 questions before moving to the next. A hand rail will help guide you along the path. A ball at the end of each hand rail will signify a change of hand rail from right to left or left to right. White cane detectable stone edges shall guide your direction on the path. A bell at the end of each rail will signify an easy to find seating area to answer your Q&A.
educational.p1:
Ecology:
Working together...
Important fun Facts on route

Culture and History: Identifying cultural and historical foods and practices from Inca to us.
Seed preparation: cultivation, storage and why we must protect them for future generations.
Soil: Soil preparation, Composting, Microbes and care.
Insects: Pollination, Beneficial species and natural pest management.
Animal Input: Sources from other beneficial animals.
Plant Care: Plant relationships, Identifying disease and management.
Replanting:  Cycles of harvesting, helping the ecosystems, environmental help.
Harvesting: When, why and how.
Global Impact: Looking at new and old data to prepare for changes.
Water Management: Water testing, Identifying problems, New solutions, Cleaning and maintenance, Preserve and protect.
Replanting: Cycles of harvesting, environmental help.
Animal Care: Understanding how animals play a big role in supporting the cycle of life, from plowing the fields to animal waste. Learning to listen and sense their behaviors.
Community: Working with others, relationships, Supporting and  sharing.
educational.p3: Healthy soil grows healthy plants. Healthy plants feed healthy people. The educational trail is that idea, told as a path you can walk.

sensory.title: Sensory trail — {siteName}
sensory.description: A walk of touch, scent, sound and the ground underfoot, for blind and visually impaired visitors and the people beside them.
sensory.heroLine: On this path you learn to identify and use the plants. All downloaded as you go to use in the future.
sensory.heroAlt: A bearded man leans close to leafy green plants, seen from the side. Only the lower edge of his glasses shows at the top.
sensory.lead:
Download the app: Then the experience begins.Feel or see the Braille Map layout from beginning to end
Two options:
1: Visually Impaired: Audio version
2: SIghted: QR/NFC scan at stations..
All Junction points have Braille information cards.
Visually Impaired: Audio version

On this sensory path you will experience the many wonders and aromas the Apus (Mountain Spirits) and Pachamama (Mother Earth) nourish us with. There will also be QR/NFC markers provided with detailed information about individual plants, traditional, medicinal, culinary and personal care uses and how to prepare them.All this information you will be able to take away with you so you can refer to it at any time.
The main reason is that I personally have visited many information trails and wasn't able to retain the information or i wrote things down and  lost the information over time, but now you can refer to it when ever needed.
Enjoy :)
sensory.p1: On the sensory trail, people are invited to walk slowly and meet this place with the body. A rope handrail leads the way. Stone, wood, leaves and flowers are there to be touched. Herbs and damp earth offer scent. Water, birds and wind offer sound.
sensory.p2: The ground changes under the feet, from stone to soil, so each step says where you are. Nothing on this walk depends on sight.
